parts.title: Part I – Multiple Choice Questions
parts.instructions: Part I contains 35 questions. Each question carries 2 points. Use g = 10 m/s² and c = 3×10⁸ m/s as printed on the paper.

questions.stem: In some state of matter the molecules are oscillating near their points of equilibrium and cannot move freely in any direction. Which state of matter satisfies this condition?

options.A: A gas
options.B: A solid
options.C: A liquid
options.D: A fluid
options.E: A vapor

explanation_steps: In a solid, molecules vibrate about fixed equilibrium positions and cannot move freely.
Gases and vapours move freely; liquids can flow. A fluid means liquid or gas. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which of the following has the largest number of significant figures?
explanation_steps: 203, 24.2 and 0.130 each have 3 significant figures; 0.0900 has 3 (leading zeros do not count).
10.00 has 4 significant figures because the trailing zeros after the decimal are significant. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Which one of the following contains two vector quantities and a scalar quantity?

options.A: Distance, acceleration, speed.
options.B: Displacement, velocity, force.
options.C: Distance, mass, speed.
options.D: Displacement, velocity, speed.
options.E: Mass, time, work.

explanation_steps: Displacement and velocity are vectors; speed is a scalar.
A has one vector; B has three vectors; C and E are all scalars. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the linear motion of an object with constant velocity?

options.A: Distance from the initial position is a linear function of time.
options.B: Velocity is a linear function of time.
options.C: Distance from the initial position is a quadratic function of time.
options.D: Acceleration is a non-zero constant.
options.E: Acceleration is a linear function of time.

explanation_steps: Constant velocity means a = 0 and s = vt, so distance from the start grows linearly with time.
Velocity is constant, not a changing linear function, and acceleration is zero. Answer: A.

questions.stem: A body starts from rest and acquires a velocity of 10 m/s in 5 s. What are the acceleration of the body and the distance traveled by it during this time interval?

options.A: 4 m/s², 20 m
options.B: 2 m/s², 25 m
options.C: 2 m/s², 40 m
options.D: 2 m/s², 20 m
options.E: 2 m/s², 10 m

explanation_steps: s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½×2×25 = 25 m. Use g only where needed; here motion is given by the speed change. Answer: B.

questions.stem: A freely falling object is dropped from a tower and hits the ground with a speed of 20 m/s. What is the height of the tower in m? (Use g = 10 m/s².)
explanation_steps: Dropped: u = 0. v² = u² + 2gh ⇒ 400 = 2×10×h ⇒ h = 20 m. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?

options.A: The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is tangent to the circle.
options.B: The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is constant in magnitude.
options.C: The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is directed toward the center of the circle.
options.D: The velocity of a particle in a uniform circular motion is perpendicular to its acceleration.
options.E: The acceleration of a particle in a uniform circular motion is constant in magnitude.

explanation_steps: Velocity in uniform circular motion is tangential, not toward the centre. The centripetal acceleration points to the centre.
A, B, D and E are true. The incorrect statement is C.

questions.stem: A motorcar having a mass of 1000 kg accelerates by a net force of 2000 N from rest. What is the speed of the car after 10 seconds (in m/s)?
explanation_steps: From rest, v = at = 2×10 = 20 m/s. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Car A is traveling at 60 km/h due north and another car B is traveling at 70 km/h due south. The velocity of car B relative to A is

options.A: 10 km/h south.
options.B: 130 km/h south.
options.C: 65 km/h north.
options.D: 10 km/h north.
options.E: 30 km/h north.

explanation_steps: Take north as positive: v_A = +60 km/h, v_B = −70 km/h.
v_B relative to A = v_B − v_A = −130 km/h, that is 130 km/h south. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Choose the wrong statement from the following.

options.A: The total work done on an object is equal to the change in kinetic energy.
options.B: The work done on an object is always positive.
options.C: The kinetic energy of a moving object is always positive.
options.D: When the speed of an object is doubled its kinetic energy quadruples.
options.E: Work and energy have the same units.

explanation_steps: Work can be positive or negative depending on the angle between force and displacement.
A is the work–energy theorem; C, D (KE ∝ v²) and E are true. The wrong statement is B.

questions.stem: A particle moving horizontally with a velocity of 10 m/s starts to move up along a frictionless surface (Figure 1). The maximum height h (in meters) the particle will reach is
explanation_steps: On a frictionless rise, ½mv² = mgh, so h = v²/(2g).
h = 10²/(2×10) = 5 m. Answer: C.

questions.stem: A force of 10 N acts on a 2 kg block (initially at rest) placed on a frictionless horizontal surface for 5 seconds (Figure 2). The change in momentum of the block (in kg·m/s) is
explanation_steps: Impulse equals change in momentum: Δp = FΔt = 10×5 = 50 kg·m/s.
The mass is not needed because the force and time are given. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is correct for an image formed by a plane mirror?

options.A: The image is real.
options.B: The image is magnified.
options.C: The image is inverted.
options.D: The image and the object distances from the mirror are always different.
options.E: The left hand of the object appears as the right hand in the image.

explanation_steps: A plane mirror gives a virtual, same-size, laterally inverted image with equal object and image distances.
Only E is correct. Answer: E.

questions.stem: If a ray of light goes obliquely from water to air, then the value of the angle of refraction compared to the value of the angle of incidence is

options.A: Larger than the angle of incidence.
options.B: Always less than the angle of incidence.
options.C: Equal to the angle of incidence.
options.D: Not related to the angle of incidence.
options.E: Less or equal to the angle of incidence.

explanation_steps: Water has a higher refractive index than air, so an oblique ray bends away from the normal.
Therefore the angle of refraction is larger than the angle of incidence (until the critical angle). Answer: A.

questions.stem: A spherical convex mirror with an object placed at a distance equal to the radius of curvature (R) from the surface of the mirror produces

options.A: A virtual image behind the mirror at a distance equal to the radius of curvature.
options.B: A virtual, diminished image behind the mirror at a distance less than the radius of curvature.
options.C: A real, magnified image at a distance equal to half of the radius of curvature.
options.D: A virtual, magnified image at a distance equal to the radius of curvature.
options.E: A real, erect image at a distance equal to half of the radius of curvature.

explanation_steps: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image behind the mirror, with |v| < |f| and f = R/2, so the image distance is less than R.
It does not form a real image for a real object. Answer: B.

questions.stem: Secondary colors are colors formed by the combination of various primary colors. Which of the following gives the correct combination?

options.A: Blue + Red = Magenta
options.B: Blue + Green = Yellow
options.C: Blue + Yellow = Cyan
options.D: Red + Yellow = Green
options.E: Green + Red = Cyan

explanation_steps: Additive primaries: red + blue = magenta, red + green = yellow, blue + green = cyan.
Only A is the correct combination. Answer: A.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of forces holds neutrons and protons together in a nucleus?

options.A: Force of gravitational interaction
options.B: Force of electric interaction
options.C: Force of magnetic interaction
options.D: Force of weak interaction
options.E: Force of strong interaction

explanation_steps: The strong nuclear interaction binds protons and neutrons in the nucleus and overcomes proton repulsion.
Gravity is far too weak; the weak interaction governs some decays. Answer: E.

questions.stem: The electrostatic force between two point charges when separated by 10 cm is 1.2 N. What will be the force (in newtons) if they are brought to a separation of 5 cm?
explanation_steps: Coulomb force is proportional to 1/r².
Separation is halved, so the force is multiplied by 4: 1.2×4 = 4.80 N. Answer: E.

questions.stem: A net charge of 30 C passes through a cross-sectional area of a wire in 2.0 minutes. What is the current in the wire (in amperes)?
explanation_steps: I = Q/t. t = 2.0 min = 120 s.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect about heat transfer?

options.A: Gases are poor conductors of heat.
options.B: Metals are good conductors of heat.
options.C: Transfer of heat by convection occurs only in fluids.
options.D: Heat is transferred from the Sun to the Earth mainly by radiation.
options.E: Conduction takes place by mass movement of heated particles.

explanation_steps: Conduction transfers energy by particle collisions, not by bulk mass movement. Mass movement is convection.
A–D are accepted statements. The incorrect one is E.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is correct about an isothermal process?

options.A: It occurs at constant pressure.
options.B: It occurs at constant volume.
options.C: It occurs with no heat flow into or out of the system.
options.D: It occurs at constant temperature.
options.E: It occurs at constant pressure and temperature.

explanation_steps: Isothermal means constant temperature.
Constant pressure is isobaric, constant volume isochoric, and no heat flow is adiabatic. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.A: A heat engine is a device that changes thermal energy into mechanical work.
options.B: A temperature difference is required to run a heat engine.
options.C: A refrigerator takes heat from a high temperature area and releases it to a low temperature area.
options.D: Heat does not flow spontaneously from a cold object to a hot object.
options.E: Heat flows naturally from a hot object to a cold object.

explanation_steps: A refrigerator removes heat from the cold region and rejects it to the hotter surroundings, using work.
C reverses that direction, so it is incorrect. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Pressure is the product of force and area.
options.B: A pressure of 1 atmosphere is equivalent to 1 newton per square meter.
options.C: The standard atmospheric pressure is roughly 760 mm Hg.
options.D: A manometer is a device used for measuring atmospheric pressure.
options.E: Atmospheric pressure increases as altitude increases.

explanation_steps: Standard atmospheric pressure is about 760 mm Hg (1.01×10⁵ Pa).
Pressure is force per area, 1 atm is not 1 Pa, a barometer measures atmospheric pressure, and pressure falls with altitude. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which statement is not true about absolute pressure at a depth h in an open liquid column?

options.A: The absolute pressure depends on the acceleration due to gravity.
options.B: The absolute pressure depends on the liquid’s density.
options.C: The absolute pressure is independent of the shape of the liquid’s container.
options.D: The absolute pressure is independent of the atmospheric pressure on top of the column.
options.E: The absolute pressure is independent of the area of the container.

explanation_steps: Absolute pressure is P = P_atm + ρgh, so it depends on atmospheric pressure.
D is therefore not true. A, B, C and E follow from that relation. Answer: D.

questions.stem: Choose the incorrect statement.

options.A: A body sinks in a liquid if its weight is more than the weight of the displaced liquid.
options.B: A body rises in a liquid if its weight is less than the weight of the displaced liquid.
options.C: A body sinks in a liquid if the buoyant force is more than the weight of the body.
options.D: A body floats in a liquid if its weight is equal to the weight of the displaced liquid.
options.E: The apparent weight of a body floating in a liquid is zero.

explanation_steps: A body sinks when its weight exceeds the buoyant force (weight of displaced liquid), not when buoyancy is larger.
If buoyancy exceeds weight the body rises. C is incorrect. Answer: C.

questions.stem: A sound wave is passing through a tube where the area of the cross-section is 2 cm² and the intensity of the wave is 4 W/m². What is the area (in cm²) of the cross-section of the tube in that place where the intensity of the same wave is 0.5 W/m²? Assume that there are no energy losses.
explanation_steps: With no energy loss, power P = IA is constant, so A₂ = A₁ I₁/I₂.
A₂ = 2 × (4/0.5) = 16 cm². Answer: B.

questions.stem: The speed of a sound wave is 330 m/s and the wavelength is 330 cm. What is the period of the sound wave in milliseconds?
explanation_steps: T = 1/f = 0.01 s = 10 ms. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is incorrect about waves?

options.A: In a transverse wave, particles of the medium vibrate perpendicular to the direction of motion of the wave.
options.B: Mechanical waves do not propagate through vacuum.
options.C: Sound wave is a transverse wave.
options.D: The speed of electromagnetic waves is much greater than that of mechanical waves.
options.E: Waves can carry energy from one place to another.

explanation_steps: Sound in air is a longitudinal wave: particles oscillate along the direction of travel.
C is incorrect. A, B, D and E are true. Answer: C.

questions.stem: A man standing in front of a high wall hears the echo of his voice after 2 s. If the speed of sound is 330 m/s, his distance to the wall in meters is
explanation_steps: The echo travels to the wall and back, so 2d = vt = 330×2 = 660 m.
d = 330 m. Answer: B.

questions.stem: The device which measures the distance to an object by measuring the time required for a radio wave to reach the object and return is called

options.A: laser.
options.B: sonar.
options.C: radar.
options.D: ultrasonic scanner.
options.E: tomograph.

explanation_steps: Radar uses radio waves and the round-trip time.
Sonar and ultrasonic scanners use sound; a laser uses light. Answer: C.

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements is correct about electromagnetic waves?

options.A: All electromagnetic waves are affected by electric and magnetic fields.
options.B: All electromagnetic waves propagate as uniform electric and magnetic fields perpendicular to each other.
options.C: All electromagnetic waves cannot be polarized.
options.D: All electromagnetic waves propagate through vacuum with speeds proportional to their wavelengths.
options.E: Electromagnetic waves can show interference and diffraction.

explanation_steps: Electromagnetic waves are transverse waves and show interference and diffraction.
They are oscillating, not uniform, fields; they can be polarized; and in vacuum they all travel at c, not at a speed proportional to wavelength. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Line spectra

options.A: cannot be used to identify elements.
options.B: can be produced by low-density monatomic gases and vapour.
options.C: can be produced by high-density monatomic gases and vapour.
options.D: can be produced by high-density diatomic gases and vapour.
options.E: can be produced by high-density polyatomic gases and vapour.

explanation_steps: A hot low-density monatomic gas emits a line spectrum characteristic of the element.
High-density sources tend to give continuous or broadened spectra. Line spectra are used to identify elements, so A is false. Answer: B.
